newsitem.title: UK: Doubts on Thorn prospects erode share gains.
newsitem.headline: Doubts on Thorn prospects erode share gains.

text.p: Question marks about prospects for electricals rentals group Thorn Plc took the shine off its proposal on Wednesday to hand shareholders 87 million stg via a share buy-back, retail analysts said.

Thorn's shares had perked up after news of the cash handout, gaining as much as 11 pence at one stage. But worries about the fundamentals of the group's rentals business in Britain and the U.S., where its performance has been poor, eroded the gains. The shares were five pence higher at 155 pence by 1220 GMT.
Analysts said nervousness about Thorn's competitive position going forward continued to overshadow the stock.

They said they believed profit forecasts for the current year had been revised down by about 10 million stg in the light of the results, but the range was quite wide - between 120 and 150 million stg.
Thorn earlier reported flat pretax profits for the year to end March 1997 of 171 million stg, its first set of full year results since it parted company from music giant EMI Plc last year.
Analysts said the demerger had exposed the weakness of the Thorn format. The shares started trading last August above 400 pence.
